Judgment
1.

Vide this judgment, I propose to dispose off the appeal filed by the appellant against the
impugned order dated 02.01.2020 whereby the Ld. Adjudicating Officer/Additional District
Magistrate(Shahdara), Delhi ("A.O." in short) imposed a penalty of Rs.25,000/ u/S 52 of The Food
Safety and Standards Act, 2006 ("Fss Act" in short) upon the appellants.

2.  The facts in brief are that on 31.01.2018 at about 4.30pm, Sh.Ram Pratap Singh, Food Safety Officer( "FSO" in short) alongwith Dr.P.M.Kothekar, Designated Officer and Sh.Subedar Mishra, the then Field Assistant visited M/s Singhal Enterprises, A64/2, East Nathu Colony, Mandoli Road,
Shahdara, Delhi110093 for inspection.
After inspection of the said shop, a sample of "Ghee" for analysis was taken.

The sample consisted of 4x1 litre of "Ghee" Madhusudan Brand (ready for sale)
in original sealed condition having identical label declaration.

Thereafter, the sample food article was divided into four equal parts and each counterpart of the sample was separately packed,
fastened and sealed according to the provisions of The Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 ( "FSS Act" in short).
Thereafter, one counterpart was sent to the Food Analyst for analysis on 01.02.2018.

sentences.text: 3. Without going into the further merits of the case, Sh.Kapil Sharma, Ld.Counsel for the appellant has submitted that the present complaint is barred by limitation.

It has been submitted that the sample in the present case was taken on 31.01.2018 and the complaint was filed on 27.06.2019 and there was no order of extension granted by The Commissioner of Food Safety.
4. Sh.Kundan Lal, Ld.Chief PP for respondent has submitted that there is no order of The Commissioner of Food Safety regarding extension of limitation.

5. Section 77 of FSS Act reads as under:
"77. Time limit for prosecutions. Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, no court shall take cognizance of an offence under this Act after the expiry of the period of one year from the date of commission of an offence:
Provided that the Commissioner of Food Safety may, for reasons to be recorded in writing, approve prosecution within an extended period of up to three years."
6.

The bare perusal of Section 77 of FSS Act makes it clear that the Ld.A.O. could not have taken cognizance of an offence after the expiry of period of one year from the date of inspection unless extension granted by The Commissioner of Food Safety.
I consider that without going into other grounds, the complaint having been filed beyond period of limitation, the Ld.A.O. should not have taken the cognizance.
Hence, the impugned order dated 02.01.2020 cannot sustain in the eyes of law and is therefore, set aside.
7. In view of the discussion made, the appeal is allowed accordingly.
8. TCR be sent back alongwith copy of the judgment.
9. Appeal file be consigned to Record Room.
